currentContext.business: The Company is primarily engaged in the business of trading of Plastic Products and states it does not have any other reportable business segments or diversified product categories, so its entire financial and operational performance is attributable to this single line of activity. Trading operations are focused on meeting customer demand through timely procurement and supply of quality plastic products, with the Company saying it continues to strengthen business relationships with suppliers and customers to ensure consistency in supply and service. Originally incorporated on 21.09.1994 as Innovations International Exim Limited and later renamed Innosoft Technologies Limited, it took its present name Innocorp Limited vide a fresh certificate of incorporation dated 16.03.2006; its equity shares have been listed on BSE since 14.08.1996.

currentContext.expansion: The Company discloses no capex, capacity addition or expansion project of any kind. It is an asset-light, single-segment trader of plastic products with two permanent employees on its rolls, and management explicitly rules out investing behind the business, stating in the MD&A that any investment and expansion in the present line of Plastics will not provide any better results; it says instead that it has continued its effort in product innovation considering changing consumer preference. The only forward-looking growth language in the report is (a) the MD&A Outlook, which says the Company is diversifying its presence in the rural market through a strong distribution network and is also exploring the potential in the international market, neither with a project, site, quantum or timeline attached; and (b) the Scheme of Reduction of Share Capital in the AGM notice, which is a balance-sheet restructuring rather than a capex programme - the Board states the Scheme is expected to strengthen the financial profile by restoring net worth and improving the ability to access equity and debt capital, 'thereby supporting its future growth and business expansion', and that it would enable the Company to raise funds through equity issuances (preferential allotments, rights issues, QIPs) or debt financing 'thereby supporting future expansion plans, operational growth and business development, which is presently constrained due to the erosion of its net worth'. The Scheme is expressly stated to involve no outflow of funds and to leave business operations, assets and liabilities unaffected. No plant, warehouse, site or machinery is named anywhere in the routed text.
currentContext.mdna: Industry structure is under pressure: management says the industry is facing lots of constraints, that margins are reduced to the lowest level, and that stiff competition from the un-organized sector and local players has adversely affected turnover.|Management is hopeful that this fiscal the Company will achieve good turnover as the economy witnesses an upward trend and good business, despite huge competition in wholesale prices and having to trade with fewer margins to sustain in the market.|Opportunity framed at the policy level: the government of India is trying to set up economic reforms to elevate and boost the plastic industry through joint venturing and foreign investments.|Environmental regulations and plastic waste management infrastructure are named as the major challenges faced by the Company.|Rural distribution reach and an as-yet-unquantified international market opportunity are the two stated growth avenues in the Outlook section.

risks.risk: Cut-throat competition from the unorganized small-scale sector and new entrants
risks.note: This is the only item the MD&A lists under 'Risks and Concerns': 'Competition from the unorganized small scale sector via cut-throat competition from the new entrants in the market, thereby squeezing the Company's profit margins.' The Industry Structure section reinforces it - stiff competition from the un-organized sector and local players 'adversely affected the turnover'. As a pure trader with no manufacturing asset, the Company has little to defend against price-led entrants.

risks.risk: Structural margin compression across the industry
risks.note: Management states the industry 'is facing lots of constraints' and that 'margins are reduced to lowest level', and expects to keep 'doing trading with fewer margins to sustain in the market' despite huge competition in wholesale prices. Margin is the binding constraint on the business, not volume.

risks.risk: Environmental regulation and plastic waste management infrastructure
risks.note: Named in the MD&A Opportunities and Threats section as 'the major challenges faced by the Company'. As a plastics trading business, tightening plastic-waste rules affect the products it can source and sell; the Company says only that it is making all its efforts to meet environment compliance and adopting various policies to avoid plastic waste, with no quantified programme disclosed.

risks.risk: Single-activity concentration - one business line, no diversification
risks.note: The MD&A states the Company 'is primarily engaged in the business of trading of Plastic Products. It does not have any other reportable business segments or diversified product categories', so 'the entire financial and operational performance is attributable to the trading of Plastic Products'. The Directors' Report confirms no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures as on 31st March 2026 and no change in the nature of business during FY 2025-26. There is no second earnings stream to absorb a shock in plastics.

risks.risk: Management has ruled out investment in the core business, leaving no organic growth path
risks.note: 'The management is of the view that any investment and expansion in the present lying of Plastics will not provide any better results.' The only stated growth avenues - diversifying into the rural market through a distribution network and exploring the international market - carry no project, quantum or timeline, so the reinvestment case in the existing line is explicitly disowned by management itself.

risks.risk: Accumulated losses large enough to require a court-sanctioned capital reduction, with execution risk on the Scheme
risks.note: The AGM special resolution seeks to cancel and extinguish 75% of the paid-up equity share capital and apply the entire Securities Premium Account to write off accumulated losses carried on the balance sheet as at 31.03.2026. The Scheme is conditional on a shareholder special resolution, on confirmation by the Hon'ble NCLT Bench at Hyderabad under Sections 66 and 52, and on filing of the certified Order and Tribunal-approved minute with the ROC - so the restoration of net worth is not within the Company's sole control and is not yet effective.

risks.risk: Macro and regulatory exposure across domestic and overseas markets
risks.note: The MD&A cautionary statement enumerates the factors that could make a material difference to operations: 'economic conditions affecting the domestic market and the overseas markets in which the Company operates, changes in the Government regulations, tax laws and other statutes and other incidental factors.' This is relevant because the stated growth plan involves entering international markets the Company does not yet serve.

risks.risk: Compliance and disclosure infrastructure gap flagged by the secretarial auditor
risks.note: The MR-3 Secretarial Audit Report for FY 2025-26, while otherwise reporting compliance, records the observation that 'the Company is not maintaining the functional website from time to time' - a live LODR disclosure-infrastructure gap noted by an independent professional, and material for a company that is simultaneously asking shareholders to approve a capital reduction whose documents it says are available on that website.

- The MD&A cautionary statement enumerates the factors that could make a material difference to operations: 'economic conditions affecting the domestic market and the overseas markets in which the Company operates, changes in the Government regulations, tax laws and other statutes and other incidental factors.' This is relevant because the stated growth plan involves entering international markets the Company does not yet serve.
